Live-action sports cinematography of an athlete during a boxing training session on a heavy bag. Real-time athletic motion, documentary sports footage.

FRAMING — HOLD THIS. The framing must stay essentially as it starts for the entire shot: the athlete on the left, the large black heavy bag filling the right edge of the frame. The heavy bag stays visible on the right side of the frame from the first frame to the last frame. The bag never leaves the frame. The athlete never leaves the frame. Both the athlete and the bag remain in shot at all times.

CAMERA. The camera is almost locked off. It creeps forward toward the athlete by only a very small amount across the whole six seconds — a barely perceptible push-in, a few percent closer at most — carried on a handheld rig, so there is only faint breathing-level unsteadiness from the operator's hands. The camera does not pan. It does not drift or track sideways. It does not move right. It does not orbit, crane, tilt, zoom, rack focus or roll. It does not close in on the athlete's face. Keep the same medium-shot scale throughout: chest and head at the top of frame, cropped at the thighs, feet out of frame.

ACTION. The shot continues from the moment the athlete's training glove meets the heavy bag. The leather of the bag compresses where the glove rests against it, then the bag swings a short distance away from him and rotates slowly on its chain, its weight carrying it through a slow, heavy pendulum arc, and swings back. The athlete draws his lead hand back to his guard. His rear foot pivots on the ball, his hips rotate, his rear shoulder comes forward and his arm extends last as he performs a second clean straight training punch — the glove reaching the bag and making contact with it, never punching empty air. Every punch in this shot lands on the bag. Fine chalk dust lifts off his wrist wraps on contact and drifts through the light. Sweat glistens and shifts across his shoulders and forearms as the muscles work. His head stays behind his guard, his eyes stay on the bag, his chest rises and falls as he breathes hard from exertion. Two clear, well-spaced punches across the six seconds — deliberate technical repetitions, not a fast flurry. Between them the guard returns and he resets his stance.

LIGHTING — HOLD THIS. The gym stays dim and underexposed for the entire shot. The lighting does not change, does not brighten, and does not bloom. The background stays dark and falls away into deep shadow. The distant window stays a small, dim, cold patch of pale dawn light — it must never grow, never blow out to white, and never flood the frame with daylight. Keep the single cold directional key from camera right and slightly behind, raking his shoulder, arm and cheekbone and skimming the near face of the bag. Keep the desaturated cool-neutral grade, the deep crushed blacks, the warm skin tone as the only saturated element, the shallow depth of field with the athlete in critical focus, and the fine film grain. Low-key, high-contrast, dawn interior.

PHYSICS. The bag is heavy and swings like a heavy object — slow, weighted, plausible on its chain, never rubbery or floaty. Anatomy must hold through the fastest frames of the motion: two arms, two hands, correct elbows, correct shoulders, training gloves keeping their shape and volume. Nothing warps, stretches, morphs or duplicates.

Do not add any other person. Do not add text, subtitles, captions, logos, signage or watermarks at any point. No slow motion. No speed ramping.
